newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says balanced budget deal "imperative".
newsitem.headline: Clinton says balanced budget deal "imperative".

text.p: President Bill Clinton, meeting with bipartisan congressional leaders, said on Tuesday it was "imperative" to reach a balanced federal budget agreement this year.

Democrat Clinton said his invitation to visit the Republican-led Congress to discuss the budget and other issues was "an important first step" toward bipartisan negotiation. At the outset of the meeting, he told reporters: "I think it indicates we want to work together. I just want to emphasise too, that I think it is imperative that we pass a bipartisan balanced budget this year."

Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, a Mississippi Republican, said there were areas of agreement between Congress and the White House such as the need to balance the budget, provide tax relief and ways to deal with education, drugs, crime and the environment.
"Rather than come together and argue on the things we disagree on we thought that (it would be) an opportunity to begin to identify issues where we can work together," he said.

House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich, who tangled with Clinton in budget battles over the past two years, said it was important to reach a bipartisan agreement to balance the budget and achieve education reform this year. "We think it is a chance for us to have a real dialogue," said Gingrich, a Georgia Republican.

The top congressional Democrats -- Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle of South Dakota and House Minority Leader Richard Gephardt of Missouri -- attended as did other leaders from both parties. Administration officials who accompanied Clinton included White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles, Office of Management and Budget Director Frank Raines, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and Education Secretary Richard Riley.
